options.reason: Absolute counts directly show the number of motorist and cyclist deaths in each year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; the count gap ranged from 51 in 2019 to 115 in 2021, and 2025 had 81 motorist deaths versus 23 cyclist deaths.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how many motorist and cyclist deaths occurred in each requested year; the bars show more motorist deaths in every year, with the smallest absolute gap in 2019 and largest in 2021. options.metric: Annual ratio of motorist deaths to cyclist deaths
options.denominator: Cyclist deaths in the same calendar year
options.reason: The ratio makes the relative scale of motorist and cyclist death counts comparable across years.
options.answer: Motorist deaths were 2.6 times cyclist deaths in 2019 (the lowest ratio) and 10.0 times in 2013 (the highest); the 2025 ratio was 3.5.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the relative number of motorist deaths compared with cyclist deaths changed year by year: the ratio ranged from 2.6 in 2019 to 10.0 in 2013, and was 3.5 in 2025. A same-year ratio is a defensible way to compare relative counts when the groups have different totals, but it does not show the absolute size of the death counts or death risk per traveler.
